District of Columbia: what's on the November 3, 2026 ballot

Every candidate below is listed alphabetically, with party shown as text only. Open a name for their stated positions, background and recent news, each with sources.

Open District of Columbia on the map

Key dates

  • Voter registration deadline (mail and online): October 13, 2026. This is the deadline for applications that are not submitted in person. You can still register in person at Early Vote Centers (Oct. 26 to Nov. 1) or at Vote Centers on Election Day.
  • Last day to request a mail ballot: October 19, 2026. Ballot requests must be received by this date (15 days before the election). The Board planned to mail ballots to all registered voters starting about Sept. 28. Mailed ballots must be postmarked by Election Day and received by Nov. 13. Drop boxes close at 8:00 p.m. on Election Day.
  • Early voting at Early Vote Centers: October 26, 2026 to November 1, 2026. Open every day from 8:30 a.m. to 7:00 p.m. You can register and vote at the same visit.
  • Election Day: November 3, 2026. Vote Centers are open 7:00 a.m. to 8:00 p.m. Anyone in line at 8:00 p.m. may vote, and you can register at a Vote Center that day.

Official election information: vote.gov

Ballot measures

Initiative Measure No. 86: Prohibiting Force-Feeding of Birds Act of 2026

Bans force-feeding a bird to enlarge its liver beyond normal size, and bans selling or distributing products made this way, including foie gras. The Department of Energy and Environment would enforce it during routine food safety inspections, with civil penalties.

Yes: A yes vote approves the initiative, making it illegal in the District to force-feed birds this way or to sell or distribute products made from force-fed birds, such as foie gras, with civil penalties.
No: A no vote rejects the initiative, leaving current law unchanged, so this force-feeding ban and foie gras sales ban would not take effect.
